questions.stem: Which of the following is true when two lines are parallel?
choices: They intersect at exactly one point.
questions.solution: When two lines are parallel, they never meet. This is a basic property of parallel lines. The other options are incorrect because parallel lines do not meet at any point, they have the same slope, and they intersect at only one point if they are not parallel.

hi.solution: जब दो रेखाएं समांतर होती हैं तो वे कभी मिलती नहीं हैं। यह समांतर रेखाओं के एक मूलभूत गुण है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि समांतर रेखाएं किसी भी बिंदु पर मिलती नहीं हैं, वे समान ढलान रखती हैं, और वे केवल एक बिंदु पर प्रतिच्छेद करती हैं यदि वे समांतर नहीं होती हैं।

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes two lines that never meet, even when extended?
questions.solution: Parallel lines are defined as lines that lie on the same plane and never meet, even when extended infinitely in both directions. Intersecting lines meet at a point, perpendicular lines meet at a right angle, and skew lines are not on the same plane and do not intersect. Hence, the correct answer is parallel lines.

questions.stem: In the given figure, if line l is parallel to line m, and line n is a transversal intersecting them, which of the following is true?
questions.solution: When a transversal intersects two parallel lines, corresponding angles are equal. This is a fundamental property of parallel lines and transversals. The other options are incorrect because alternate interior angles are equal, not supplementary, consecutive interior angles are supplementary, and vertical angles are equal, not complementary.

questions.stem: If a transversal intersects two parallel lines and forms corresponding angles, what can be said about these corresponding angles?
questions.solution: Corresponding angles formed by a transversal intersecting two parallel lines are always equal due to the geometric properties of parallel lines. Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees, and complementary angles add up to 90 degrees, neither of which is a requirement for corresponding angles. Different angles would not maintain the parallel relationship between the lines.

questions.stem: In a diagram, two lines intersect and form four angles. If one angle is 135°, what is the measure of the angle adjacent to it?
questions.solution: Adjacent angles formed by intersecting lines are called linear pairs and always add up to 180°. If one angle is 135°, the adjacent angle will be 180° - 135° = 45°. The other options are incorrect because 135° is the vertically opposite angle, 90° is a right angle, and 180° is a straight angle.

hi.stem: एक आरेख में, दो रेखाएं एक दूसरे को काटती हैं और चार कोण बनाती हैं। यदि एक कोण 135° है, तो इसके समीपवर्ती कोण का माप क्या होगा?
hi.solution: काटती हुई रेखाओं द्वारा बने समीपवर्ती कोण रैखिक युग्म कहलाते हैं और हमेशा 180° के बराबर होते हैं। यदि एक कोण 135° है, तो समीपवर्ती कोण 180° - 135° = 45° होगा। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि 135° लंबवत विपरीत कोण है, 90° एक समकोण है और 180° एक सीधा कोण है।

questions.stem: In Fig. 5.14, if line t is a transversal that intersects lines l and m, and it is observed that ∠1 and ∠5 are corresponding angles, what can be concluded about lines l and m?
choices: They intersect at an acute angle
questions.solution: If corresponding angles formed by a transversal are equal, the lines cut by the transversal must be parallel. Since ∠1 and ∠5 are corresponding angles and are assumed to be equal, this confirms that lines l and m are parallel. Perpendicular lines would create right angles, which is not indicated here. Skew lines exist in three dimensions and are not relevant in this two-dimensional scenario.

questions.stem: In the given figure, line a is parallel to line c. If ∠1 = 52°, what is the value of ∠2?
questions.solution: Since line a is parallel to line c and a transversal intersects them, ∠1 and ∠2 are consecutive interior angles. According to the property, consecutive interior angles add up to 180°. If ∠1 is 52°, then ∠2 = 180° - 52° = 128°. The other options are incorrect because 52° would be the measure of a corresponding angle, 180° is not a valid angle in this context, and 90° is the measure of a right angle, which is not related here.

hi.stem: दिए गए आकृति में, रेखा a रेखा c के समांतर है। यदि ∠1 = 52°, तो ∠2 का मान क्या है?
hi.solution: क्योंकि रेखा a रेखा c के समांतर है और एक तिर्यक रेखा इनको काटती है, ∠1 और ∠2 अंतः समांतर कोण हैं। गुण के अनुसार, अंतः समांतर कोणों के मानों का योग 180° होता है। यदि ∠1 52° है, तो ∠2 = 180° - 52° = 128°। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि 52° एक संगत कोण के माप के रूप में होगा, 180° इस संदर्भ में एक वैध कोण नहीं है, और 90° एक समकोण के माप के रूप में होगा, जो यहां संबंधित नहीं है।

questions.stem: In a scenario where a transversal intersects two lines and forms two distinct angles, what condition must be met for the lines to be parallel?
choices: The two distinct angles must be equal
The two distinct angles must be supplementary
The two distinct angles must be complementary
The two distinct angles must be acute
questions.solution: For lines to be parallel when intersected by a transversal, the corresponding angles formed must be equal in measure. This is a fundamental geometric principle. Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees, which is not a requirement for parallelism, and complementary angles add up to 90 degrees, which is also not relevant. Acute angles are simply angles less than 90 degrees and do not determine parallelism on their own.
